Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above? 

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=3$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=3$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. As $x$ approaches $0$ from the left and right we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{-}}f(x)=3,\,{lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}\,.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=\text{DNE}.$

- Statement II is false. We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)=\text{DNE},\,{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)=3\,.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}.$

- Statement III is true.  We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x)=2
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=2.$ Meanwhile, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x)=2
$$

 
Hence ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=2.$ Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x).$

In conclusion, only statement III is true.

Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above? 

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=4$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,3}f(x)=1$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x)=3\,.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=3.$

- Statement II is true. Both limits ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)$ do not exist because the function $f(x)$ is not given in the interval $(0,2].$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}\,.
$$

- Statement III is true. We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{3}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{3}^{+}}f(x)=1\,.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,3}f(x)=1.$

In conclusion, only statements II and III are true.

The function  $y=f(x)$ is defined on $x\in (-\frac{5}{2},3).$ Find ${lim}_{x\to \,3}f(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
From the graph, we see that it is not possible to approach $x=3$ from the right. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{3}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

When we approach $x=3$ from the left, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{3}^{-}}f(x)=0\,.
$$

Since ${lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}f(x),$ we  conclude  that
 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,3}f(x)=\text{DNE}\,.
$$
